ops.entry: WHEN a product distill run must reach a borrowed plan reader DO dispatch harness-code-reviewer with HARNESS-MISSION: distill — dispatch-guard now places the lead by its own registered distill run, so older distill digests recording that refusal are stale precedent, not a reason to skip the reader.
ops.why: The product-lead to code-reviewer distill dispatch ran without refusal in this run; earlier product distill digests record it as refused and the reader's lesson undelivered.

ops.entry: WHEN assessing or relaying a cited line DO open the enclosing function, not just the grep hit — a pointer can be sound while its prose gloss is wrong, and a grep hit confirms the text but not which code path owns it.
ops.why: I relayed a ruling's gloss 'writer at :870' after grepping the line; the member opened it and found it inside release_cmd, not the claim writer, and narrowed the entry. Old P-02 already said open a cited line; the grep-hit-vs-enclosing-function gap is the sharper rule.

ops.entry: WHEN apply remediates a high plan-reader finding and the team runs no re-read step DO put it to the operator as one blocking signature question with a recommendation, naming applied text that prescribes literal commands or gate-read literals as unread — a signer's re-read grades substance, not rendering.
ops.why: Outcome of following O-10: the signer accepted the applied remediations as re-read, and validate later found the applied printed repair commands unrunnable as printed (bare script, punctuation adjoining a path, unquoted). The question had not flagged literal text as the unread risk.

originals.original: WHEN assessing a member's cited evidence DO open at least one cited line rather than counting them — a pointer can be sound while the prose gloss of it is wrong, and a pointer's whole value is that it survives being opened.

WHEN apply remediates a high plan-reader finding and the team runs no re-read step DO put it to the operator as one blocking signature question with a recommendation instead of re-spawning the reader — an overrule-as-applied costs no spawn, and the run's FAIL still records the unread gap.
